title: How Emmanuel Macron brought France’s AI darling to the world stage
content:
Mistral has forged unrivaled ties with the French presidency. Now, Emmanuel Macron is departing.

By OCÉANE HERRERO
in Paris

Illustrations by Björn Griesbach for POLITICO

It’s not every AI company that can count the French president as its top salesman.

On June 11, 2025, the founder of French AI company Mistral took to the stage alongside Jensen Huang, the powerful CEO of chip giant Nvidia, to announce a partnership between the two companies. As President Emmanuel Macron joined them, the Taiwanese-American executive turned to Mistral’s young CEO Arthur Mensch and said something just audible to the Parisian audience of techies and public officials: “Your president worked really hard for you.”

The Nvidia boss was referring to the deal his company had just sealed with Mistral to roll out AI infrastructure across Europe. “I told the president that Arthur and Mistral needed support from France’s biggest companies. Mr. President said to me: ‘Which ones? Let me call them!’” Huang said.

title: Lebanon: New media law makes progress but leaves serious free expression gaps
content:
Following years of advocacy by civil society organisations, journalists and activists, Lebanon has passed a new media law that introduces important human rights-based reforms, but falls short of bringing all the changes needed to ensure that the right to freedom of expression is respected, protected and fulfilled in the country, Amnesty International said today.  

The Lebanese Parliament adopted a long-awaited Media Law on 11 August 2026 replacing outdated legislation from 1962 and 1994. The law published in the official gazette on 3 September, introduces several long-overdue safeguards for journalists, media workers and people exercising their right to freedom of expression online, including decriminalizing insults and defamation in some instances, introducing stronger protections for sources, prohibiting pretrial detention in media-related cases, restricting military court jurisdiction for such cases, and expanding protections for online expression.

title: Baha’i Citizen Vafa Kashefi Sentenced to Six Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, Vafa Kashefi has been sentenced to prison.

According to a ruling issued by the Mashhad Revolutionary Court and communicated to Kashefi, he was sentenced to five years in prison on the charge of “assembly and collusion with the intent to disrupt social security” and one year in prison on the charge of “propaganda against the regime.”

Two and a half years of the total sentence have been suspended. Under the ruling, if the verdict is upheld, the most severe applicable punishment, two and a half years in prison, will be enforced against this Baha’i citizen. He was also acquitted of the charges of insulting the Supreme Leader and inciting people to participate in unrest.

Kashefi’s court hearing was held on August 29, 2026, at the Mashhad Revolutionary Court. He remains incarcerated in Vakilabad Prison.

Vafa Kashefi was arrested on April 21, 2026, after reporting to the Mashhad Prosecutor’s Office and was transferred to Vakilabad Prison.

The approximately 32-year-old Baha’i citizen had previously been arrested at his home on January 11, 2026, and was released on bail after approximately one week.

title: Kaupunkien liikenneympäristöt ovat tärkeitä elinpaikkoja monille kasveille ja pölyttäjille
content:
Kaupunkien liikenteenjakajissa, parkkipaikoilla ja tienpientareilla menestyvät etenkin kasvilajit, joilla on keltaiset tai suuret kukat ja joita pistiäiset pölyttävät.

Kaupunkiympäristöön kuuluu monenlaisia viheralueita aina metsistä ja niityistä puistoihin ja viherkattoihin. Näiden lisäksi viheralueverkostoa täydentää liikenneympäristöihin liittyvä kasvillisuus, joka muodostaa omanlaisensa elinympäristön. 

Tällaiset viheralueet ovat kaupungeissa hyvin tyypillisiä, mutta niiden ekologista merkitystä pölyttäjien elinympäristöinä on tutkittu verrattain vähän. 

Turun yliopiston biologian laitoksen tutkijat toteuttivat kasvillisuuskartoituksen Helsingissä, Turussa ja Tampereella kesällä 2022. Tutkijat tarkastelivat liikenneympäristöjen viheralueita, eli liikenteenjakajia, parkkipaikkoja ja tienpientareita.

title: Unlocking knowledge: diamond open access publishing - UNESCO Digital Library
content: Diamond Open Access (OA) is an equitable scholarly publishing model that treats knowledge as a digital public good, with no fees for readers or authors. Built on shared infrastructure, open licensing, and community governance, it supports non-profit, academically driven publishing while allowing commercial providers to deliver specific services. Like Open Educational Resources (OER), Diamond OA promotes equitable access, collaboration, and multilingual knowledge sharing. It can strengthen national and institutional Open Access strategies while connecting OER, Open Data, and open research software into interoperable knowledge ecosystems. This brief examines Diamond OA infrastructure and provides practical policy guidance for Member States and institutions.

title: The Remnants of a Lost ‘Supercontinent’ Just Rewrote the History of Life on Earth
content:
Scientists have identified the submerged remnants of a giant lost supercontinent that played a pivotal role in the explosion of complex life more than 500 million years ago, reports a study published on Wednesday in Science Advances.

By gathering over 25,000 rocks from ancient continental fragments, a team reconstructed the past contours of Gondwana, a massive landmass that formed between 800 and 500 million years ago in the Southern Hemisphere. Gondwana’s true size has long been a matter of contentious debate, but it is generally thought to have taken up two-thirds of Earth’s land at the time, falling short of “supercontinent” status.

Now, scientists led by Tao Wang, a professor of geoscience at the Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences, have revealed that Gondwana accounted for roughly 80 percent of Earth’s landmass between 550 and 500 million years ago, confirming that it was a supercontinent.

title: 2026 EFF Award Winners: Access Now, 7amleh – The Arab Center for the Advancement of Social Media, DeFlock, and New Media Rights
content:
EFF is pleased to announce that Access Now, 7amleh – The Arab Center for the Advancement of Social Media, DeFlock, and New Media Rights have received 2026 EFF Awards for their vital work in ensuring that technology supports freedom, justice, and innovation for all people. 

The EFF Awards recognize specific and substantial technical, social, economic, or cultural contributions in diverse fields including journalism, art, digital access, legislation, technology development, and law. 

For the past 30 years, the EFF Awards—previously known as the Pioneer Awards—have recognized and honored key leaders in the fight for freedom and innovation online. Started when the internet was new, the Awards now reflect the fact that the online world has become both a necessity in modern life and a continually evolving set of tools for communication, organizing, creativity, and increasing human potential.

title: Lebanon/Israel: Hezbollah’s Use of Cluster Munitions
content:
(Beirut, September 9, 2026) – Hezbollah unlawfully fired widely banned cluster munitions into a town in northern Israel on March 4, 2026, and again on March 15, Human Rights Watch said today. 

The attacks, neither of which caused civilian casualties, took place during a major escalation in the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah beginning on March 2 as part of the wider war in the region involving Iran and the United States.

“Cluster munitions should not be used under any circumstances, and their use may amount to a war crime,” said Patrick Thompson, crisis, conflict and arms researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Not only are they inherently indiscriminate, but unexploded submunitions can kill and injure civilians long after hostilities conclude.” 

Cluster munitions are fired in rockets, missiles, and projectiles, or dropped from aircraft. They typically disperse in the air, spreading dozens of explosive submunitions, or bomblets, indiscriminately over a large area. Many fail to explode on initial impact, leaving duds that can kill and maim, like landmines, for years or even decades, unless cleared and destroyed.

title: Suomeen harhautuneissa drooneissa räjähteitä – vain yksi räjähti pudotessaan
content:
Suomeen keväällä tulleet ja maahan pudonneet ilma-alukset eli droonit olivat lähtöisin Ukrainasta, vahvistui keskusrikospoliisin (KRP) ja Rajavartiolaitoksen esitutkinnoissa.

Esitutkintojen perusteella droonit olivat osa Ukrainan vastatoimia, jotka johtuivat Venäjän hyökkäyssodasta.

Suomen maaperältä löytyi keväällä neljä droonia, joista ensimmäiset kolme maaliskuun lopulla Kouvolasta, Luumäeltä ja Parikkalasta Pyhäjärven jäältä. Myöhemmin huhtikuussa myös Päijät-Hämeen Iitistä löytyi drooni.

KRP:N ja Rajavartiolaitoksen mukaan tutkinnassa saadun selvityksen perusteella ilma-aluksia ei ollut kohdennettu Suomeen, vaan niiden harhautumiseen vaikuttivat voimakas GNSS-häirintä Suomenlahden itäosissa sekä vallinneet sääolosuhteet. Näiden tekijöiden arvioidaan vaikuttaneen droonien suunnistamiseen ja niiden poikkeamiseen alkuperäiseltä reitiltä.

Rajavartiolaitos tutki tapahtumia epäiltyinä alueloukkauksina ja KRP epäiltyinä törkeinä yleisvaaran tuottamuksina sekä yleisvaaran tuottamuksena. Tutkinnan aikana yhteistyötä tehtiin muun muassa Ukrainan viranomaisten kanssa.

title: 2 miljoonaa euroa arktisen alueen murroksen ja mielen kansanterveyden tutkimukseen Helsingin yliopiston tutkijoille
content:
The Strategic Research Council, which operates under the Research Council of Finland, has granted a total of 24 million euros for research that will explore changes in the Arctic region and mental health in Finnish society.

Funding went to eight consortia, four of which include researchers from the University of Helsinki. The six-year programmes are now getting under way and will run until autumn 2032.

The Changing Arctic Region (ARCTIC) programme examines the ongoing, multi-layered changes in the Arctic region that result from climate change, geopolitical tensions and economic interests. The research projects will engage in close dialogue and cooperation with regional actors such as local and Indigenous communities. The University of Helsinki is involved in two of the programme's consortia.

The  project treats Arctic security as something that takes shape at the meeting point of the state, public institutions, civil society, and local and Indigenous communities. It responds to a global polycrisis that in the Arctic shows up as rapid climate change, intensifying military competition and shifting levels of trust.

title: Oulun tuomiokirkossa huippumäärä kävijöitä – kirkkoon tutustui kesän aikana lähes 29 000 vierailijaa
content:
Oulun tuomiokirkon viime kesä oli kävijämäärän osalta ennätyksellisen vilkas, sillä kirkossa vieraili yhteensä 28 914 henkilöä. Edelliskesänä kävijöitä oli 15 762 ja sitä edeltäneenä kesänä 10 634. Päiväkohtainen kävijäennätys rikkoutui 22. kesäkuuta, kun Ouluun rantautuneelta risteilijältä saapui kirkkoon 1 462 vierailijaa.

Kävijöistä noin puolet oli suomalaisia. Suomen lisäksi vierailijoita oli 48 eri maasta, eniten Saksasta ja Puolasta. Kävijöitä saapui myös muun muassa Yhdysvalloista, Ruotsista, Kiinasta, Japanista ja Norjasta.

Tuomiokirkon oppaiden esihenkilönä toimiva seurakuntamestari Timo Rantala arvioi vierailijamäärän kasvun johtuvan Oulun kulttuuripääkaupunkivuodesta ja sen puitteissa järjestetyistä tapahtumista. Tuomiokirkossa kesän vetonauloina olivat The Logos -äänitaideteoksen lisäksi Kirkolliset aarteet -näyttely sekä ukrainalaisia ikoneita esitellyt Icons on Ammo Boxes -näyttely.

title: US lawmakers urge Congress to act after AI researcher’s dire warning
content:
Lawmakers in Washington from both parties are escalating pleas for legislative action after an artificial intelligence researcher claimed late Tuesday that unchecked AI models could feasibly destroy the world by the decade’s end — and AI developers know it.

While it’s not the first time experts have warned of the existential threats posed by an unregulated industry that is rapidly advancing, it comes at a moment of heightened awareness on Capitol Hill about the need to reach consensus on AI safety legislation before it’s too late.

“The call is coming from inside the house,” Rep. Lori Trahan of Massachusetts, a House Democrat seeking to lead her party on AI policy, posted on X Wednesday. “Safety researchers are resigning, powerful AI models are breaking out of their labs, and companies are racing ahead anyway.”

She was responding to social media posts from former Anthropic AI researcher Jason Coxon, whose warnings were first reported in the Wall Street Journal.

title: “Racial violence is accelerating and we must resist”
content:
Liliane Umubyeyi co-founded African Futures Lab in a bid to rewrite the narrative around Africans and people of African descent and to ensure they receive the reparatory justice they deserve.

Now, as anti-right movements become the norm and racial violence around the world accelerates, she wants to remind people that there’s a movement of people fighting back, calling for reparations and holding those in power to account….


Politics has always been a part of my life.

As a young child in Rwanda, I remember there being a violent political climate preceding the 1994 Rwandan genocide against the Tutsi. By the time I was 10, we were forced to flee following the genocide.

We travelled to Kenya, on to Cameroon where I learnt French, before settling in Belgium, where we were Black African refugees.

After studying law, taking on a PhD and working for differing human rights organizations, including the UN, I began to see a disconnection between human rights and racial justice. I could see the impact of colonialism in terms of how the organizations I was working for resolved problems – they had a Eurocentric way of thinking when it came to how political and legal systems should work.

title: Babak Moradifar Sentenced to 30 Months in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, political activist Babak Moradifar announced that he had been sentenced to 30 months in prison.

In a video, Babak Moradifar stated that Branch 28 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Amouzad, sentenced him at the initial stage of proceedings to 30 months in prison.

According to the indictment issued by Branch 2 of the Evin Prosecutor’s Office, he was charged with “assembly and collusion with the intent to disrupt national security through propaganda activities against the Islamic Republic.” His attendance at a ceremony marking the seventh day after Khosrow Alikordi’s death in Mashhad and his support for the January 2026 protests were cited among the grounds for the charge.

On the morning of January 9, 2026, Moradifar was arrested by Ministry of Intelligence agents at his home in Tehran. According to a previous HRANA report, following his arrest, his family had no information about his condition or whereabouts for ten days, until he informed them in a brief phone call that he was being held in Evin Prison.

title: White Phosphorus: Recent Use, Inhumane Effects Require New Law
content:
(New York, September 9, 2026) – Recent use of white phosphorus munitions by Israeli forces in Lebanon underscores the need for new international law to regulate these devastating weapons, Human Rights Watch and the International Human Rights Clinic at Harvard Law School said in a report released today. The groups urged countries to take up the issue at the United Nations General Assembly’s monthlong disarmament meeting in New York in October 2026.

The 45-page report, “Uncontrolled Burn: The Inhumane Effects of White Phosphorus Munitions and the Need for Stronger Law,” documents 23 verified incidents of Israeli use in southern Lebanon between March and May 2026. The report also details the horrific harm the munitions have caused in armed conflicts in recent years. White phosphorus munitions, which produce fire when their payload is exposed to oxygen, are not currently regulated by a specific treaty.

title: Ammattikuljettajilta jyrähdys hallitukselle – ”Kestämätön taso”
content:
Ammattiautoilijat vaativat Petteri Orpon (kok.) hallitusta puuttumaan kestämättömiksi nousseisiin polttonesteiden hintoihin. Ne katsovat hintojen vahingoittavan Suomen taloutta.

Asiasta tiedottaa Liikenne Suomi-ryhmä eli Suomen Kuljetus ja Logistiikka SKAL, Linja-autoliitto ja Taksiliitto.

Tavara- ja henkilöliikenteen yritykset kärsivät tiedotteen mukaan voimakkaasti energian hinnasta. Vain noin puolessa vuodessa dieselin hinta on noussut yli 50 senttiä litralta ja ylittää paikoin jo 2,50 euroa.

YKSINOMAAN tavaraliikenteen kuljetusyrityksille kustannusnousu merkitsee Liikenne Suomi -ryhmän mukaan vuositasolla jopa 480 miljoonan euron lisälaskua. Jos ammattiliikenteen kustannukset nousevat liikaa, rakentamisen, kaupan ja teollisuuden kustannukset kasvavat ja yksityisten kuluttajien liikkuminen vaikeutuu.

Suomen naapurimaat ryhtyivät tiedotteen mukaan toimeen jo keväällä, kun energiahinnat lähtivät nousuun.

– Suomi oli logistisella takamatkalla jo sitä ennen, muistuttaa SKALin puheenjohtaja Jari Välikangas.

title: US allies lack resources to keep pace on AI, top Pentagon official says
content:
Cameron Stanley talks up ‘revolutionary’ AI capabilities and says Washington working with Nato and Five Eyes partners

The Pentagon’s top artificial intelligence official said on Tuesday that America’s closest allies lack the resources to keep pace with the US military’s adoption of AI, and that Washington is working to steer them away from mistakes it made along the way.

“They don’t have the resources that we do, they don’t have the experience that we do, they don’t have the scale that we do,” Cameron Stanley, chief digital and artificial intelligence officer at the Department of Defense, said at an event at the Billington Cybersecurity summit. Of Nato and the Five Eyes, an intelligence-sharing partnership of the US, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, Stanley said Washington was “actively working with a number of our partners” so “they don’t make the same mistakes that we make”.

title: Yhdenvertainen ja esteetön Suomi -palkinto Lakeuden Elämysliikunnalle
content:
Invalidiliitto on myöntänyt Yhdenvertainen ja esteetön Suomi -palkinnon Lakeuden Elämysliikunta ry:lle pitkäjänteisestä työstä esteettömän ja yhdenvertaisen luontoliikunnan edistämiseksi. Kunniamaininnan saivat WAM nykytaiteen museo Turussa ja Serlachius-taidekohde Mäntässä.

Lakeuden Elämysliikunta ry:llä on vuosikymmenten kokemus esteettömien ja saavutettavien luontoympäristöjen, reitistöjen ja palvelujen kehittämisestä. Yhdistys on ollut mukana lähes 50 hankkeessa, joissa esteettömyys, saavutettavuus ja yhdenvertainen osallisuus ovat olleet keskeisiä teemoja.

Toiminnan kantavana ajatuksena on, että luonto kuuluu kaikille. Esteettömyys nähdään laajasti mahdollisuutena päästä luontoon, osallistua, kokea elämyksiä ja nauttia luonnon hyvinvointivaikutuksista riippumatta ihmisen toimintakyvystä, iästä, elämäntilanteesta tai taustasta.

title: EU seeks to transform procurement into €600B driver of industry
content:
BRUSSELS — The EU wants to transform public procurement into a powerful tool of industrial policy by channeling hundreds of billions of euros spent on infrastructure, schools, energy or health toward European businesses.

In its Public Procurement Act unveiled on Wednesday, Ursula von der Leyen’s Commission is following up on recommendations by economic reform guru Mario Draghi to give a lift to struggling European industry while shielding the bloc from external risks in an increasingly uncertain world.

The sums involved are huge. Public procurement represents up to 15 percent of the EU’s GDP — or around €2.5 trillion a year. Of that, some €600 billion is governed by EU rules, Executive Vice President Stéphane Séjourné told reporters.

“This is public money, which must also serve our collective goals,” the French commissioner said. “It’s the equivalent of a yearly recovery plan and about four to five times the EU budget in terms of spending.”

title: Kodin tietoliikenne vuonna 2035: Nämä teknologiat vaativat verkolta eniten
content:
Tulevaisuuden kodissa nettiä eivät tarvitse vain älypuhelimet ja tietokoneet, vaan koko elinympäristö. Älykodin sensorit optimoivat lämmitystä ja ilmanvaihtoa sähkön pörssihinnan mukaan reaaliajassa, ja kodin turvallisuusjärjestelmät analysoivat korkearesoluutioista videokuvaa tekoälyn avulla.

Todellinen testi verkolle on kuitenkin samanaikainen käyttö. Arki-iltana tavallisessa taloudessa saatetaan elää tilannetta, jossa yksi perheenjäsen osallistuu virtuaalipalaveriin, toinen pelaa viiveetöntä pilviurheilupeliä ja olohuoneessa pyörii saumattomasti 16K-resoluution suoratoisto. Samaan aikaan taustalla raksuttavat lukuisat henkilökohtaiset tekoälypalvelut, jotka vaativat jatkuvaa datavirtaa.

Yhä edelleen verkon datanopeuksissa tuijotetaan usein vain latausnopeutta kotiin päin (download). Vähintään yhtä tärkeää on kuitenkin lähetysnopeus (upload). Symmetrinen datayhteys tarkoittaa, että download ja upload ovat yhtä nopeita. Valokuitu on ainoa tiedonsiirron tekniikka, joka tarjoaa aidosti symmetrisen yhteyden – aina. Siksi ei ole samantekevää, millä tekniikalla data siirtyy.

title: OpenAI claims to have solved maths problem that stumped humans for decades
content:
Company behind ChatGPT says 10,000 of its AI systems cracked the Navier-Stokes problem in 88 hours

OpenAI claims to have solved a major mathematics problem that has stumped humans for nearly a century after spending millions of dollars on the artificial intelligence-led endeavour.

The company behind ChatGPT said it had cracked the Navier-Stokes problem, one of seven Millennium Prize Problems published by the Clay Mathematics Institute to highlight some of the biggest unsolved puzzles in the field.

title: From Checklists to Crisis Response: CODATA and UNESCO Present the First Global Survey on Data Policies for Times of Crisis
content:
Crises rarely wait for institutions to be ready for them. Floods, epidemics, earthquakes and displacement events unfold across borders, sectors and time zones, and the organisations that respond to them succeed or fail depending on whether they can find, trust and share the right data fast enough. That simple observation sits at the heart of the Data Policies for Times of Crisis (DPTC) Toolkit, developed jointly by UNESCO and the International Science Council’s Committee on Data (CODATA), and it was the common theme of two sessions to which CODATA contributed at the 2026 Global Conference of the International Decade of Sciences for Sustainable Development (IDSSD) in Paris: the ISC session on 16 July ‘Resilient Science for Resilient Societies: Protecting Knowledge and Scientists in Times of Crisis’, and the dedicated UNESCO–CODATA thematic session on 17 July ‘Data policies for times of crisis: Enabling open science for coordinated response’.

Two sessions, one message

title: Up Close and Personal with the Trump Administration’s NIH Funding Cuts: An Interview with Sylvia Chou and Alexa Romberg - The Scholarly Kitchen
content: "More than 400,000 US federal employees have left their jobs during the second Trump administration – voluntarily or, in many cases, not. Even taking into account new hires since January 2025, there has been a net loss of 285,000 staff, many of whom had years, if not decades, of experience. Over 10,000 of them were experts in STEM and health fields, with the National Institutes of Health (NIH) especially hard hit, losing more than 1,100 staff – around 10% of its workforce. Among them were Sylvia Chou and Alexa Romberg, who chose to leave the organization as a result of the changes being made under NIH Director Dr Jay Bhattacharya. They were two of the original signatories of the Bethesda Declaration, an open letter to Dr Bhattacharya that expressed serious concerns about the changes being made under his leadership. Sylvia and Alexa are both involved in 27 UNIHTED (Sylvia as a Senior Advisor), an organization that was set up in 2025 as a way to continue supporting the integrity of publicly-funded health research in the United States. title: Lukutaitopolitiikka on myös kulttuuripolitiikkaa
content:
Kansainvälistä lukutaitopäivää vietetään 8. syyskuuta tänä vuonna jo 60. kerran. UNESCO julisti päivän vuonna 1966, ja vuoden 2026 teemana on Literacy for people, the planet and prosperity.

Suomella on päivään erityinen suhde. Olemme edelleen maailman lukutaitokärkeä: OECD:n viimeisimmässä aikuisten taitoja mittaavassa PIAAC-tutkimuksessa suomalaiset saavuttivat vertailumaiden parhaan keskimääräisen tuloksen lukutaidossa. Samaan aikaan 12,4 prosenttia 16–65-vuotiaista suomalaisista sijoittuu lukutaidossa tasolle 1 tai sen alapuolelle. Nämä kaksi asiaa voivat olla totta yhtä aikaa. Suomen vahva keskiarvo kertoo vuosikymmenten onnistuneesta sivistyspolitiikasta, mutta sen rinnalla on joukko ihmisiä, joiden mahdollisuudet toimia yhä monimutkaisemmaksi muuttuvassa informaatioympäristössä ovat selvästi muita heikommat. Ja juuri informaatioympäristö on muuttunut.

title: Minna Canth -palkinto jaetaan jälleen yhdenvertaisuuden ja demokratian edistäjälle - palkinto motivoi viime vuoden voittajaa jatkamaan tärkeää työtä
content:
Jopa 35 000 € arvoinen Minna Canth -palkinto jaetaan taas ensi keväänä. Esityksiä palkinnon saajaksi otetaan parhaillaan vastaan – ehdotukset tulee jättää 29.9.2026 mennessä. Palkinto jaetaan vuosittain henkilölle tai taholle, joka on toiminnallaan edistänyt yhdenvertaisuutta, sananvapautta ja tukenut demokratiaa.

Tunnustus kantaa kuopiolaisen kirjailijan, yhteiskunnallisen vaikuttajan ja tasa-arvon puolestapuhujan Minna Canthin nimeä. Tavoitteena on palkinnon avulla nostaa esiin toimijoita, jotka edistävät Canthille tärkeiden arvojen toteutumista.

Viime vuonna palkinnon sai Nicehearts ry, joka järjestää toimintaa ja tukipalveluita tytöille, naisille ja perheille. Yhdistys edistää toiminnallaan yhdenvertaisuutta, osallisuutta ja yhteisöllisyyttä tukemalla tyttöjen, naisten, perheiden ja sukupuolivähemmistöjen mahdollisuuksia löytää oma paikkansa yhteiskunnassa.

Nicehearts ry:n toiminnanjohtaja Johanna Sjöholmin mukaan palkinnon saaminen merkitsi paljon niin yhdistykselle kuin kävijöillekin.

– Palkinnossa on sellainen positiivinen painolasti, se motivoi jatkamaan tätä työtä eteenpäin, Sjöholm sanoo.

title: 29.9.26 Conferenza: La più antica biblioteca conosciuta in Hispania

Villa Lante al Gianicolo, Passeggiata del Gianicolo 10
Ingresso libero fino ad esaurimento posti

Dott. Antonio López García
Università di Granada

Come si può riconoscere una biblioteca romana quando i libri e gli arredi sono scomparsi? Partendo dalla recente identificazione della più antica biblioteca finora conosciuta in Hispania, nella villa romana di Fuente Álamo (Puente Genil, Córdoba), la conferenza mostrerà come l’integrazione di analisi architettonica, statistica e confronti archeologici possa rivelare la funzione di spazi rimasti a lungo enigmatici.

title: Frank Lloyd Wright’s Secret Career as a Japanese Art Dealer & How It Shaped His Architecture
content:
Frank Lloyd Wright was often strapped for cash. In that respect, he had something in common with Vincent van Gogh, who passed most of his much shorter life in more dire circumstances. Unlike Wright, who enjoyed decades of fame at the pinnacle of the American architectural profession, van Gogh remained practically unknown until after his death. But if they’ve encountered one another in the afterlife, they’ve certainly discussed one subject above all others: their shared appreciation for Japanese woodblock prints. Here on Open Culture, we’ve previously featured the collection of 500 such works of art that van Gogh left behind. At the end of Wright’s life in 1959, he owned about 6,000, many of which his estate had to sell to pay both Japanese art dealers and American tax collectors.

We could say that Wright died as he lived, advanced age having not evidently diminished either his financial recklessness or his obsession with ukiyo‑e. The masters of that classical “art of the floating world” like Hokusai and Hiroshige were among his favorite artists of any kind. When still a teenager, Wright went to work for the architect Joseph Silsbee, who’d built a chapel for his uncle.

title: What Can a Computer See?: Testing the Limits of Automated QA for Web Archives
content:
This blog post was co-authored by Nicky Martin, a 2026 Junior Fellow, and his mentor, Tracee Haupt Fugate, a Digital Collections Specialist in the Web Archiving Section.

Preserving a website is complicated. Even a simple webpage can depend on dozens of images, videos, scripts, style sheets, and other resources scattered across the web. Some content appears only after someone interacts with the page, while JavaScript and other technologies can make parts of a site difficult for web crawlers to discover. If some of those pieces are missed, the archived version may look or behave differently than the original.

title: The Flowers of Elizabeth Sprague Coolidge, Preserved from Another Century
content:
-This is a guest post by Nyla Adams, an intern in the Office of Communications this summer.

In 1882, a 17-year-old Elizabeth Sprague Coolidge embarked on a grand tour of Europe with her parents, traveling to nearly every country of Western Europe and attending operas whenever possible.

Coolidge kept several journals, including narrative writings and a “botanical diary” of pressed flowers and other greenery representing the places she visited.

Many years after that trip, in 1925, the pianist and composer established the Coolidge Foundation at the Library, providing support for contemporary music to continue through generations, inspiring and shaping the mission of the Library’s Music Division.

Her spectacular album of botanical specimens is a hidden gem preserved in the division’s Elizabeth Sprague Coolidge Foundation Collection, which was fully processed and made available for research last year.

“Alongside her narrative diary and photographs from her European tour, researchers have the opportunity to learn as much about Elizabeth the human as we do about Mrs. Coolidge the benefactor,” said Cait Miller, senior music reference specialist.

title: Copyright trolling: the experience of HE and related organisations
content:

To build up a more accurate picture, Tim and Liesl ran a survey. 36 organisations responded, both from within the UK and internationally. You can read the report here:

The consistent thread throughout the report is that copyright trolling is a common issue and there is a general lack of clarity about how to handle these requests. title: The Knowledge Concentration
content:
Knowledge is concentrated in the hands of a few global players based on the biggest theft in human history where they took knowledge from millions of decentralized websites and redirected the users to their own websites. Thus, there is a serious risk for other knowledge providers on the internet to become unprofitable and thereby unsustainable. 

Ever since Chat GPT, Claude and friends were made publicly available a few years back, critics have been concerned that our ability to learn and evaluate may decline once we outsource more and more of our thinking and knowing to the use of LLMs. Here on Dataethics.EU1, Olivia Heslinga has presented some of the first studies on the cognitive impact of outsourcing and offloading critical thinking skills. In short, she outlines how extended AI use over time leads to cognitive debt. Elisa Caeli discusses how the spread of AI content makes even more difficult for young people to assess the reliability of information2. Even though it is still early days both in terms of using LLMs and research on the effects thereof, the first indications are not promising for the human mind.

title: The Draghi plan at 2: Competitiveness crusade runs into Europe’s old politics
content:
BRUSSELS — Two years after Mario Draghi warned that Europe faced an “existential” threat from economic decline, his plan to make the continent competitive again has become the EU’s official agenda — but implementation lags behind rhetoric.

The Commission has proposed a series of Draghi-inspired measures, from an industrial policy overhaul to new funding for competitiveness and defense. Yet grand ambition has come up against the realities of the EU legislative machine, and many proposals remain stuck in negotiations as national governments continue to defend their spending priorities and policymaking turf.

A year ago, Draghi didn’t sound too happy with how quickly his plan was being implemented. Since then, his frustration with the lack of progress has become increasingly visible. The former Italian prime minister recently co-founded the Rhine Group with Stripe chief Patrick Collison, bringing together business leaders, economists and former policymakers to push Europe from diagnosis to action.

title: Can a new national peace policy fix Nigeria’s security problems?
content:
Nigeria's National Peace Policy is a framework intended to bring greater coordination to conflict prevention and peacebuilding

Originally published on Global Voices

ACC. H. O. Idoko, Nigeria Security and Civil Defense Corps (NSCDC) representative, speaking at the National Peace Policy review in Abuja, 4-6 August, 2026. Photo by Triple Peace Africa. Used with permission.

The world is spending more on war and defense than ever before. Global military expenditure reached a record USD 2.7 trillion in 2024, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), as governments increased spending amid wars in Europe and Western Asia and growing security tensions elsewhere. 

Africa is part of that trend. Military expenditure on the continent rose by 8.5 percent in 2025 to USD 58.2 billion. Nigeria’s spending rose even more sharply, increasing by 55 percent to USD 2.1 billion, according to SIPRI.

title: South Korea: Systemic Gender, Age Discrimination at Work
content:
(Seoul) – Women in South Korea face systemic gender discrimination at every stage of their working lives, Human Rights Watch said in a report released today. These adverse impacts accumulate as women get older, and are compounded by systemic age discrimination, resulting in harm to their physical and mental health.

The 92-page report, “Too Old and a Woman: Systemic Age and Gender Discrimination Against Women at Work in South Korea,” documents that social attitudes toward education, unfair treatment in hiring, disrupted careers due to family responsibilities, limited promotion opportunities, glass ceilings, and sexual harassment create a disadvantage for South Korean women throughout their working lives. As women get older, their work opportunities narrow to a handful of low-paid, insecure jobs, and the gender pay gap increases. By the time they are eligible for pensions, women face a significant gender pension gap.

title: Earthquakes and Japan: Does Preparedness Truly Equal Prevention?
content:
By Kadhija Mohamed

TOKYO | 8 September 2026 (IDN) — This past couple of months, our planet has seen a seemingly significant rise in the number of higher magnitude earthquakes in regions near tectonic fault lines all over the world.

Last month alone there were devastating earthquakes with a magnitude of five or higher in Egypt, the Philippines, Colombia, Indonesia, and Japan. The country most affected by earthquakes this year was Venezuela, which was hit by twin earthquakes, respectively with magnitudes of 7.2 and 7.5, claimed the lives of over 6000 people this June.

Other developing nations that were hit this year such as Colombia, the Mindanao region of the Philippines and Afghanistan, while not as severely, also reported over a hundred casualties in addition to serious damage to their infrastructure. What is shocking, however, is the fact that this number of great earthquakes is in fact normal and within range for the predicted number of earthquakes annually.

title: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster
content:
Foreign minister Shisir Khanal tells the Guardian the world’s biggest economies need to help Nepal, which contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions

Nepal is demanding $20m in climate compensation for the recent devastating floods, as a senior minister called on the world’s most polluting countries to “wake up” and accept shared responsibility for a disaster that led to the death or disappearance of more than 6,000 people.

Scientists believe the climate crisis had a role to play in the floods, which were triggered when a melting glacier partially collapsed and set off a deadly landslide and flash flooding through Chinese-controlled Tibet and Nepal in late August. So far, more than 1,300 are confirmed dead and more than 5,500 still missing, with hopes of their survival diminished after 12 days of rescue operations.

The Slovak government on Wednesday evening blocked the extension of sanctions targeting those undermining Ukraine’s territorial integrity, which apply to more than 3,000 Russian individuals and companies, according to Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda and Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL).

At the time, the EU’s Committee of Permanent Representatives (Coreper II) was discussing the extension of the sanctions, but reportedly failed to reach an agreement because of Slovakia.

Foreign media reported that Slovakia is insisting that the sanctions not be extended for a year, as the Irish presidency is now proposing, but only for six months, as has been the case until now.

Slovakia is also reportedly seeking to have several names removed from the sanctions list. According to information obtained by euBrief, specifically two names are at issue.

The countries have postponed the matter until 9 September for now, but they must reach an agreement by 15 September at the latest to prevent the sanctions from expiring.

title: Channel 5 Gave Hunter Biden a List of Its Subscribers’ Emails for Some Reason
content:
Channel 5, the YouTube channel hosted by Andrew Callaghan, said it gave a list of its email subscribers to Hunter Biden, the former president’s son, who went on to promote his new memecoin, a move that a data privacy expert told 404 Media is likely illegal in some jurisdictions.

Callaghan has repeatedly interviewed Biden on camera. Apparently over the cross of that source and interviewer relationship, Biden “asked if he could use our mailing list whenever he launched a new product,” according to a statement posted by Channel 5 to X on Monday. The statement said that Channel 5 did actually provide Biden with real user data: “We provided him a simple csv sheet from our email list to help him expand his audience.”

And although Channel 5 said in a follow-up statement that “emails from Hunter’s team have not gone out to any of our public subscribers,” sharing the data at all has understandably sparked a huge backlash.

It’s also probably illegal.

title: How newsrooms can learn from failure without failing in public
content:
There's a tension between journalism and product innovation, and it comes down to a clash of mental models. Journalism requires getting the facts right the first time. On the other hand, product innovation learns more from what doesn't work than from what does, and sometimes that means putting something half-baked in the wild to find out what audiences will actually respond to.

Luke Williams, a former creative director at frog design who taught my innovation and design class at NYU Stern this spring, has a line for this: be wrong at the start to be right at the end. It resonated because I've been in news organizations where the journalistic mental model is applied, often for good reasons. But when the product is held to the journalistic bar, nothing half-baked gets launched to teach us anything.

Code is now accessible to anyone with a laptop and an internet connection. The old bottleneck, engineering resources, is gone. That should mean launching more ideas, iterating faster, and learning about our audiences and our mistakes along the way.

title: Philippine Ex-Speaker Arrested in $118M Plunder Case
content:
Former Philippine House Speaker Martin Romualdez, a cousin of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., was arrested Monday after the country’s anti-graft court issued a warrant in a 7.44-billion-peso ($118 million) plunder case involving alleged kickbacks from government flood-control and other infrastructure projects.

The Philippines’ Office of the Ombudsman filed the case against Romualdez and three other defendants: former lawmaker Zaldy Co, Romualdez’s personal assistant Joselyn Tragua Serenio, and foreign exchange company president Felicito Cristobal Guevarra. The Sandiganbayan anti-graft court subsequently found probable cause and issued arrest warrants for all four, with no bail recommended.

Prosecutors allege that between 2022 and 2025, Romualdez and his co-defendants accumulated billions of pesos through commissions, kickbacks, and bribes from contractors and other entities seeking government infrastructure work. The allegations center particularly on flood-control projects, which have become the subject of a wider corruption investigation in the Philippines.

title: This State Is Spending More on Lethal Injections. A Law Tries to Keep the Details Secret.
content:
Before I joined ProPublica in 2021, I had spent a year writing about a Georgia prison physician named Carlo Musso, one of the rare doctors who’d openly talked about his role in lethal injections. After he stepped away from that work, I wanted to know who replaced him, so I filed open records requests for documents that would shed light on that. 

The role Musso held is so controversial that more than a dozen states have made it illegal to disclose the names of those involved with lethal injections. Georgia is among them. The state has gone to great lengths to hide the details around how it carries out lethal injections.  

Georgia wouldn’t release records I had requested, claiming that its secrecy law is needed to prevent those helping with its executions from getting harassed by opponents of the death penalty. 

I ended up suing the state. A few years later, a panel of three judges sided with me, and the state released some of the documents.

content:
Se tapahtui todella nopeasti. Maaliskuussa 2025, pari kuukautta Yhdysvaltojen 47. presidentin Donald Trumpin virkaanastujaisten jälkeen, noin 80 prosenttia maan kehitysyhteistyövirasto USAIDin ohjelmista oli lakkautettu.
Vuosikymmenien järjestelmät romahtivat lähes yhdessä yössä. Miljoonien ihmisten terveyspalveluiden tai lääkityksen saanti katkesi.

Yhdysvallat toteutti uutta globaalin terveyden strategiaansa, jossa tärkeintä ei ole kansainvälinen terveys, vaan Amerikan etu: America First Global Health Strategy.

Nykyhallinnolle se on merkityksellinen vain, jos se voidaan valjastaa ulkopoliittisiin tarpeisiin ja geopoliittiseen kilpailuun.

Vaikuttaa siltä, että Yhdysvallat pyrkii saamaan yksinoikeuden afrikkalaisten terveystietoihin ja patogeeneihin.

title: Suomi ja useat maat vaativat Israelia lopettamaan Länsirannan siirtokuntien laajentamisen
content:
Kanadan ja usean Euroopan valtion ulkoministerit vaativat tiistaina julkaistussa yhteislausunnossaan Israelia lopettamaan Länsirannan siirtokuntien laajentamisen.

Yhteensä 12 maan ulkoministerin lausunnossa on mukana myös Suomen ulkoministeri Elina Valtonen (kok.). Lausunnossa vaaditaan turvaamaan kahden valtion mallin mahdollisuus.

- Ennennäkemättömälle tasolle kasvanut siirtokuntalaisten väkivalta ja siirtokuntien laajentuminen heikentää tilannetta nopeasti, lausunnossa todetaan.

Lausunnossa todetaan maiden vahvistavan aikomuksensa ottaa käyttöön kansallisia pakotteita tai tukea eurooppalaisia pakotteita, jotka kohdistuvat kauppaan Israelin laittomien Länsirannan siirtokuntien kanssa.

Uusia pakotteita tiistaina esitellyt Britannian ulkoministeri Ed Miliband sanoi, että Britannia pitää siirtokuntalaisten toimintaa osassa Länsirantaa etnisenä puhdistuksena.

title: Tekoäly osaa jo suuren osan monen ammattilaisen työstä – se ei vielä tarkoita työpaikan katoamista
content:
Johanna Kohvakka

Kymmenen vuotta sitten tekoälytutkija Geoffrey Hinton julisti Toronton-konferenssissa, että röntgenlääkärien kouluttaminen kannattaisi lopettaa saman tien: kone oppisi tulkitsemaan kuvia ihmistä paremmin muutamassa vuodessa, ja ammatti häviäisi sen mukana. Myöhemmin Hintonista tuli tekoälytutkimuksen Nobel-palkittu "kummisetä", ja hänen ennustuksensa kiersi maailmaa varoituksena siitä, mitä koneoppiminen on tekemässä asiantuntijatyölle.

Kuvien tulkinta on nykyään koneelta sujuvaa. Silti röntgenlääkäreistä on Yhdysvalloissa pikemminkin pulaa kuin ylitarjontaa, ja heidän palkkansa ovat nousseet ennätyslukemiin, yli puoleen miljoonaan dollariin vuodessa. Ilmiö on herättänyt taloustieteilijöiden keskuudessa kysymyksen: miksi se, että kone oppi tulkitsemaan kuvia, ei tuhonnutkaan ammattia, jonka ydintehtävänä kuvantulkintaa pidettiin?

title: Q&A: What can – and cannot – be said about global warming’s role in the 2026 Himalayan floods
content:
• What happened?
  • How did bedrock collapse trigger the flash floods?
  • How have temperatures risen in the affected region? 
  • How have rising temperatures affected mountain stability?
  • How have glaciers retreated in the affected region?
  • Can the event be attributed to climate change?

    • On the morning of 26 August, flash floods surged through a Himalayan border region of Nepal and the Chinese region of Tibet, killing more than 1,300 people, with thousands still missing.

    In the days since the floods, scientists have examined satellite imagery, drone footage and seismic data in order to understand and explain the forces behind the event.

    While initial theories pinned the flood on a glacial collapse, scientists now understand the event as a “multi-hazard cascade”, which began with a bedrock collapse. 

    Some climate sceptics have tried to use this to falsely claim that human-caused climate change had no impact on the event. 

    Yet, scientists have noted that, while no formal attribution study has been carried out thus far, warming is making such ice-rock avalanches in the region more likely.

title: European Heritage Days 2026: protecting Europe’s heritage at risk
content:
The EU strives to preserve cultural heritage under all circumstances, as reflected in the EU preparedness union strategy. Across Europe, communities are finding diverse ways to respond to these pressures with the support of the European Union.

Throughout September and October, the European Heritage Days 2026 invites people across Europe, under the theme “heritage at risk: revive, resist, reimagine” to discover how communities are protecting, restoring and reimagining their heritage for the future.

The 2026 European Heritage Days highlight how communities and EU-supported initiatives are protecting and adapting cultural heritage in response to climate change, societal shifts and other forms of threats, including conflict.

Link to the European Heritage Days website.

As climate change increases pressure on cultural sites and landscapes through extreme weather, flooding, fires and other natural hazards, protecting heritage also means finding ways to adapt. These challenges highlight how closely Europe’s natural and cultural heritage are connected.

title: US Chips Policy Gains In Intelligence
content:
When the US enacted the CHIPS Act four years ago, the first goal was to revitalize domestic semiconductor manufacturing. Out of the $59 billion budget, two-thirds went to grants and loan guarantees for foundries. Intel and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) built plants in Arizona. Samsung invested in Texas. Micron invested in New York.

But new CHIPS Act funding pivots away from treating success as a simple count of chip production. It funds a broad range of artificial intelligence computing capabilities: advanced packaging, interconnects, memory, photonics, materials and secure electronics.

The pivot is welcome. The US will never be entirely self-sufficient in chips. Instead, it needs to build US capability at critical bottlenecks, and avoid asking US taxpayers to finance every layer of a global supply chain. If it is to meet the challenge from China, Washington needs, above all, to work with trusted democratic allies – seeing them as assets, not as dangerous competitors.

title: How ‘egalitarian’ Sweden became more comfortable with wealth
content:
Sweden is imagined as the land of equality, modesty and Jantelagen – the unwritten rule that no one should think they are better than anyone else. But there has also been a fascination within Sweden with its billionaires, especially those who abide by these dominant cultural norms.

In the case of Ingvar Kamprad, the founder of furniture giant IKEA, Swedes appreciated that he drove an old car (a Volvo, of course), engaged with employees working on the floor in his stores, and every year personally handed out Christmas gifts. His (some would say strategic) display of ordinariness made people overlook the fact that Kamprad was one of the world’s richest people and had moved to Switzerland to avoid Sweden’s high taxes.

But things have changed. The Wall Street Journal has written about Sweden’s surprising “capitalist makeover” and the Financial Times has reported on the idea the country is “overflowing with billionaires”. And in 2024 The BBC broadcast a documentary podcast called Super-rich Swedes. There are good reasons for their interest.

title: How museums can adapt their content to short-video formats
content:
For a growing share of your potential audience, the first encounter with your museum is a vertical video they did not go looking for. It arrives between a recipe and a dog, it lasts forty seconds, and it decides whether they ever think about you again.

Vertical video is now the default unit of social media. TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn, Threads and X all push it, and all of them reward organisations that make it natively rather than repurposing whatever the marketing team already had. The question is no longer whether to make short video. It is how to make it well without a production budget you don’t have.

title: New Records Reveal Problems with Medicare’s AI Prior Authorization Experiment
content: EFF sued the government back in March for information about the Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction (WISeR) model, a new Medicare program that uses AI to evaluate prior authorization requests for certain medical services. Today, we’re releasing approximately 1,000 pages of records obtained from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) through this litigation, including contracts with tech companies, internal status reports and providers’ complaints about the program. The documents (available here) show that WISeR has resulted in widespread delays and denials of care, operational chaos, and reports of patient harm.

title: Bilal Zafar Espoossa: Sähköposti kuolee viidessä vuodessa – tekoälystä tulee työelämän uusi tiedonvälittäjä
content:
Tekoälyasiantuntija Bilal Zafar ennustaa, että sähköposti sellaisena kuin sitä nykyisin käytämme muuttuu työelämässä tarpeettomaksi viidessä vuodessa. Zafarin mukaan tekoäly pystyy tulevaisuudessa käsittelemään ja välittämään tietoa suoraan oikeille ihmisille ja oikeisiin järjestelmiin. Tällöin ihmistä ei enää tarvita samalla tavalla organisaation sisäiseksi tiedon reitittäjäksi.

title: UK to force Apple and Google to block explicit images on children’s smartphones
content:
Lisa Nandy says government will introduce legislation after talks end without breakthrough

Apple and Google will be forced to block explicit images on children’s smartphones by law in the UK after talks failed to produce a breakthrough, the government has said.

The legislation commitment puts ministers on a collision course with two of the biggest players in Silicon Valley, months after the government announced a social media ban for under-16s.

title: SAMKilta uusi Resurssiviisauden osaamiskeskus – tavoitteena Suomen resurssiviisain Satakunta
content:
Tavoitteena on tehdä Satakunnasta Suomen resurssiviisain alue. Resurssiviisaudella tarkoitetaan luonnonvarojen, raaka-aineiden, energian, tuotteiden, palveluiden, tilojen ja ajan älykästä ja tehokasta hyödyntämistä. Samalla vähennetään ympäristökuormitusta, vahvistetaan kiertotaloutta ja luodaan uusia mahdollisuuksia liiketoiminnalle.

– Resurssiviisaus luo kilpailuetua kansalliseen ja kansainväliseen liiketoimintaan. Satakunnassa se tarkoittaa, että energia, ruoka, rakentaminen ja materiaalit ajatellaan kokonaisuutena: vähennetään hukkaa, pienennetään kustannuksia, luodaan sivuvirroista uusia liiketoimintamahdollisuuksia ja vahvistetaan valmiutta häiriötilanteisiin. Huoltovarmuus ei ole meillä erillinen sivujuonne, vaan se kulkee läpi kaiken osaamisemme, tutkimuspäällikkö ja keskuksen vetäjä Mikko Lehtonen tiivistää.

title: Neurowissenschaftliches Forschungsprojekt
content:
Sobald wir ein Bild sehen, einen Beitrag hören, den Duft einer Speise riechen oder einen Bericht in der Tageszeitung lesen, lösen diese Wahrnehmungen ein Feuerwerk an bioelektrischen Signalen in unserem Gehirn aus. Wie können Neurotechnologien einen Blick auf (ver-)urteilende Verstandesaktivitäten werfen? Können mediale Einflüsse unsere individuellen Entscheidungen unmittelbar mitprägen? Ein Linzer Forscher*innenteam lud Museumsbesucher*innen von 20. bis 22. Februar 2024 dazu ein, diese Fragen im temporären Neuro Experience Lab des Ars Electronica Centers zu erforschen.

Sich einer Situation zuzuwenden oder etwas von vornherein abzulehnen, sind entscheidende Aspekte für das darauffolgende, entscheidende Handeln. An mentalen Bewertungsvorgängen sind unter anderem Bereiche des präfrontalen Kortex beteiligt, die sich im vorderen Bereich des Gehirns hinter der Stirn beﬁnden. Können innere Bewertungsvorgänge im Gehirn bereits sichtbar gemacht werden? Mit der Teilnahme an der Forschungsstudie erhielten Museumsbesucher*innen die Gelegenheit, tiefe Einblicke in ihre Gehirnaktivität zu gewinnen und ihre eigenen neuronalen Antworten live zu betrachten.

title: How the Japanese Practice of “Forest Bathing”—Or Just Hanging Out in the Woods—Can Lower Stress Levels and Fight Disease
content:
When the U.S. media began reporting on the phenomenon of “forest bathing” as a therapy for mental and physical health, the online commentariat—as it will—mocked the concept relentlessly as yet another pretentious, bourgeois repackaging of something thoroughly mundane. Didn’t we just used to call it “going outside”?

Well, yes, if all “forest bathing” means is “going outside,” then it does sound like a grandiose and unnecessary phrase. The term, however, is not an American marketing invention but a translation of the Japanese shinrin-yoku. “Coined by the Japanese Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries in 1982,” writes Meeri Kim at The Washington Post, “the word literally translates to ‘taking in the forest atmosphere’ or ‘forest bathing’ and refers to the process of soaking up the sights, smells and sounds of a natural setting to promote physiological and psychological health.”

title: How the EU Commission’s second-in-command plans to take on Big Tech, Big Oil and Beijing
content:
BRUSSELS — Tax Big Oil, make Big Tech invest in renewables and protect Europe from climate disasters. Teresa Ribera’s post-summer policy wishlist isn’t short of ambitious ideas. 

In a 90-minute interview with POLITICO, the European Commission’s vice president for the green transition and competition policy discussed how she sees China, data centers, climate disaster funding, and more.

Some of her comments give a glimpse of the EU executive’s plans for the coming months, while others showcase Ribera’s own priorities. Climate change remains her top concern, and she returned throughout the interview to the recent heat waves, wildfires and drought that have ravaged Europe. “This summer has been madness,” she said. 

Two years into the job, the former Spanish ecological transition minister has also embraced the competitive aspect of her dual role, with her next big challenge being how to approach a potential breakup of search giant Google. 

Here are the five key takeaways from the interview. 

This summer has focused commissioners’ minds on the rising costs of climate change, said Ribera.

title: USA/Israel/Iran: Investigation into US-Israeli strikes on Tehran neighbourhoods reveals devastating civilian harm
content:
Deadly US-Israeli coalition attacks on densely populated areas of Tehran in March 2026, that killed and injured dozens of civilians, must urgently be independently and impartially investigated to determine whether they constitute war crimes, Amnesty International said in a new briefing published today. The organization is calling for accountability and redress for possible indiscriminate attacks in violation of international humanitarian law as hostilities continue to escalate between the USA and Iran.

The recent escalation between the USA and Iran – with reports of civilian casualties in a deadly US attack on a wedding celebration in Hormozgan province on 1 September 2026, and Iran’s retaliatory attacks on Jordan, Kuwait, Iraq and Bahrain – demonstrates that the risks to civilians across the region remain high.

The organization’s investigation into air strikes on Niloufar, Resalat, and Javadieh neighbourhoods of Tehran between 1 and 13 March 2026 found evidence that explosive weapons with wide area effects were used in densely populated areas, killing and injuring civilians and causing extensive damage to homes, businesses and other civilian buildings.

title: Kamran Hekmati, Dual-National Jewish Citizen, Released from Evin Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing Radio Farda, Kamran Hekmati was released from Evin Prison on the evening of Saturday, September 5, 2026.

According to the report, despite his release from prison, Mr. Hekmati remains subject to a ban on leaving the country and is currently in Iran.

No information has yet been released regarding the conditions of his release. However, it is believed that he may have been released after completing his prison sentence.

Mr. Hekmati has cancer. It was previously reported that he had been granted medical leave to pursue treatment. However, after approximately one month and before the end of his 45-day medical leave, he was returned to prison. His return took place before he could begin chemotherapy, raising concerns about his access to specialized medical care.

title: Russian Attacks Disrupt New School Year in Ukraine
content:
As schools in Ukraine opened for the new academic year on September 1, repeated air raid alerts in Kyiv and elsewhere have disrupted classes and sent children into shelters, sometimes for hours.

On September 3, Olya’s daughter managed to complete just one lesson – math –before alerts sent her fourth-grade class into a cramped underground shelter.

“The shelter is not equipped for studying,” said Olya, who, like others interviewed, asked to be identified by their first name, showing me a photo of the children squeezed together underground. “Even if they [teachers] wanted to continue classes, they wouldn’t be able to. It’s too noisy.”

Other subjects were assigned as homework. The children also had virtually no breaks: when an alert ended, they rushed back to the classroom to make up lost lesson time.

Recently, air raid alerts have sounded in Kyiv as many as 10 times a day, for more than five hours on some days.

Even schools with shelters equipped for classes struggle to maintain normal learning. Ira’s daughter attends a school in central Kyiv and finds shelter lessons stressful. “She cannot hear the teacher properly,” Ira said. “And there are too many people in one small space.”
snippet: As schools in Ukraine opened for the new academic year on September 1, repeated air raid alerts in Kyiv and elsewhere have disrupted classes and sent children into shelters, sometimes for hours.

title: Spanish Police Dismantle 'Dubai Bank' Narco-Network, Arrest 21
content:
Spanish authorities dismantled an international cocaine and money laundering network tied to a shadow financial system known as the "Dubai Bank," arresting 21 people worldwide and identifying 20 million euros ($23.24 million) in illicit assets, the National Police announced Tuesday.

The massive operation targeted what police described as the “aces” of global drug trafficking, including the capture of a high-value Europol target who allegedly led the Dubai-based narco-bank. Investigators said the illicit structure allowed criminal organizations to rapidly move funds across different countries to finance narcotics shipments.

Coordinated by the Special Anti-Drug Prosecutor's Office of the National Court, the investigation began in February 2021 after authorities intercepted the Nehir, a ship carrying cocaine from South America, off the Spanish coast. Officers arrested the nine-member crew and seized 1,835 kilograms of cocaine, but the vessel's captain deliberately caused a leak.

title: Suomen puolustusyhteistyö kansanmurhasta syytetyn Israelin kanssa voi kääntyä itseään vastaan, varoittavat tutkijat
content:
Suomi perustelee puolustusyhteistyötään Israelin kanssa asehankinnoilla – eli turvallisuudella. Läheinen yhteistyö kansanmurhasta syytetyn valtion kanssa sisältää kuitenkin sekä ulkopoliittisia että puolustukseen liittyviä riskejä, sanovat Ulkopoliittisen instituutin vanhempi tutkija Katariina Mustasilta ja Helsingin yliopiston väitöskirjatutkija Bruno Jäntti. 

Yle paljasti elokuun lopussa, että Suomi on solminut Israelin kanssa vuonna 2024 puolustusmateriaaliyhteistyöhön liittyvän yhteisymmärryspöytäkirjan, joka ulottuu kymmenen vuoden päähän. ”Vaikka kuinka pyrittäisiin sanoittamaan sitä niin, että nämä ovat puhtaasti puolustushankintoja, niin perustelut eivät maailmalle välttämättä mene läpi. Kyse on siitä, että tehdään merkittävää puolustusyhteistyötä sellaisen maan kanssa, jota tällä hetkellä syytetään kansainvälisen oikeuden rikkomisesta ja kansanmurhasta. title: Venäjän oppositiopoliitikko on toiveikas: sodanvastaisen Jabloko-puolueen jäsenmäärä kasvaa
content:
Venäjän ainoa julkisesti Putinia ja sotaa vastustava pikkuruinen Jabloko-puolue poistettiin elokuussa syksyn parlamenttivaalien listoilta. Puheenjohtaja Nikolai Rybakov kertoo Demokraatille, että ulosheitto on selvästi lisännyt puolueen kannatusta.

Pietarilais- tai oikeastaan leningradilaissyntyinen Nikolai Rybakov, 47, johtaa puoluetta, jonka keskeisistä vaikuttajista kahdeksan istuu vankilassa poliittisen tuomion takia.

Yli 40 puolueen tunnettua jäsentä on oikeus todennut ”ääriainekseksi” tai ulkomaiseksi agentiksi ja vienyt näin heiltä vaalikelpoisuuden.

Rybakovkin sai tuomion ”ekstremismistä”: hän oli sosiaalisessa mediassa julkaissut osanottoviestin oppositiopoliitikko Aleksei Navalnyin kuoleman takia. Se riitti äärihahmoksi leimaamiseen.

Elokuussa Venäjän korkein oikeus päätti poistaa Jablokon kokonaan 18.-20. syyskuuta pidettävien duuman vaalien puoluelistoilta.

Siitä huolimatta Rybakov kiertää nyt Venäjää kannustamassa ihmisiä äänestämään Jablokon yksittäisiä henkilöehdokkaita, joita on vielä jäljellä.

title: Alametsä: Nuorten ahdistuksesta ei voi syyttää vain vanhempia tai somea – "syyn hakeminen yksilöistä on laiskaa"
content:
Opiskelijoiden ahdistusdiagnoosit ovat kasvaneet 40 prosenttia vuodesta 2023. Vihreiden kansanedustaja Alviina Alametsä muistuttaa, ettei vastuuta nuorten mielenterveyskriisistä voi vierittää yksin nuorille tai heidän perheilleen.

Helsingin Sanomat käsitteli mielenterveyskriisin syitä viime perjantaina julkaistussa artikkelissa, jossa korostettiin ruutuajan kasvun ja ahdistuksen yhteyttä. Artikkelissa YTHS:n toimitusjohtaja Annika Saarikko pohtii kriisin taustoja ja korostaa vanhempien vastuuta kasvaneesta ruutuajasta ja sen vaikutuksista mielenterveyteen.

"Pohdinta jää mielestäni kesken. Miksi tämä ikäluokka on kasvanut ruuduilla? Yksi valtava syy on koronapandemia. Hallitus, jossa myös Saarikko oli johdossa, päätti lapsille ja nuorille todella tiukat koronarajoitukset", Alametsä muistuttaa tiedotteessa.

Alametsän mukaan kokonaiset ikäluokat pakotettiin etäkouluun ja eristettiin kotiin vuosiksi ilman kavereita ja harrastuksia.

title: The Quiet Battle Against Russia’s Shadow Fleet
content:
Ukraine’s allies have gradually persuaded flag-of-convenience states to stop providing registration for Russian ships. This quiet campaign has forced Moscow to re-flag the ships as Russian to prevent them from being seized, but that comes with a heavy financial penalty. 

A flag-of-convenience vessel can often get away with selling Russian oil in violation of sanctions at the market rate, while the false flags give service providers, buyers, and equipment suppliers plausible deniability. When ships are forced to sail under Russian colors, they cannot evade the international price cap on Russian oil, reducing the Kremlin’s income and the flow of funds for its war on Ukraine.

Flags of convenience are nothing new. Countries such as Liberia and Panama have raised revenue for decades by flagging ships with few questions asked or standards enforced. Shipping companies are attracted because they can evade safety, labor, and environmental standards, as well as sanctions

title: Afrikkalaisen sikaruton taloudelliset vaikutukset painottuvat sianlihan vientiin – peltokasvituotantoon ja metsätalouteen vaikutukset jäävät maltillisemmiksi
content:
Afrikkalaisen sikaruton (ASF) tähänastiset taloudelliset vaikutukset kohdistuvat erityisesti sianlihan vientiin, selviää Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) tuoreesta raportista. Vaikutukset peltokasvituotantoon näyttävät jäävän melko vähäisiksi. Metsätalouden rajoitusten keventäminen pienensi alun perin merkittäväksi arvioitua taloudellista riskiä.

Suomen ensimmäinen ASF-tapaus todettiin kuolleena löydetystä villisiasta Kaakkois-Suomessa Virolahdella 30. heinäkuuta 2026. Tämän jälkeen virusta on löydetty lisää samalta alueelta sekä Pyhtäältä, noin 60 kilometriä Virolahdelta länteen.

Taudin toteamisen jälkeen Suomessa otettiin käyttöön useita rajoituksia, joilla ehkäistään taudin leviämistä. Rajoitukset koskevat tartunta-alueilla toimintaa ja liikkumista sekä vaikuttavat alkutuotannon yritys- ja elinkeinotoimintaan.

Luken uudessa Afrikkalaisen sikaruton taloudelliset vaikutukset -raportissa tarkastellaan voimassa olevienrajoitusten vaikutuksia alkutuotantoon. Maatalouden osalta tarkastellaan sianlihantuotantoa ja -vientiä sekä peltokasvituotantoa. Metsätalouden tarkastelu kohdistuu mahdollisten hakkuurajoitusten vaikutuksiin puunkorjuuseen ja puunhankintaan sekä alan yrityksiin.

title: From access to impact: the gold OA advantage | Springer Nature
content:
"This white paper explores the effect of different routes to OA on the reach and impact of articles in hybrid journals. The data shows that, 8 years on from our first major study into this topic, there is still a substantial advantage for gold OA articles across all disciplines (measured by downloads, citations and Altmetric Attention Score) over both non-OA articles and green OA articles. 4

The analysis of 204,781 articles published in 1,812 hybrid Springer Nature journals in 2023 also shows how gold OA can accelerate the number of downloads over time and the diversity of geographic readership, leading to faster impact and greater equity in access."

title: Taide, elämä, filosofia –luentosarjassa suomalaiset taiteiljaryhmät 1912–1970
content:
Suomessa toimi useita taiteilijaryhmittymiä viime vuosisadalla. He suuntasivat katseensa mm. Pariisiin ja muihin kansainvälisiin vaikutteisiin ja taidesuuntauksiin sekä etsivät uudenlaista näkemystä ja tulkintaa taiteesta ja ilmaisunvapaudesta. Luentosarjan teema on suomalaisia taiteilijaryhmiä ja niiden keskeisiä vaikuttajia 1912–1970.

Tapahtuma-ajat: Keskiviikkoisin 16.9., 23.9, 14.10. 28.10. ja 11.11. klo 18-19.30

Luennoitsijat: taidehistorioitsijat Heli Haavisto ja Heta Kaisto

Ryhmä toi Suomeen värikylläisen ekspressionismin ja ranskalaista vaikutusta. Vuonna 1912 perustettu suomalainen taiteilijaryhmä toi impressionismin ja puhtaan värin käytön Suomeen. Ryhmän keskeisiä taiteilijoita olivat Magnus Enckell, A.W. Finch, Mikko Oinonen, Yrjö Ollila, Juho Rissanen, Ellen Thesleff ja Verner Thomé. Ryhmä toimi vuoteen 1917 asti.

Septemin vastavoima suosi tummaa, ekspressionistista värimaailmaa. Marraskuun ryhmä oli suomalainen ekspressionistinen taiteilijaryhmä (1917–1924), jonka keskeisiä jäseniä olivat Tyko Sallinen, Alvar Cawén, Marcus Collin, Ilmari Aalto, Mikko Carlstedt, Ragnar Ekelund, Uuno Eskola, Einar Ilmoni, Karl Ingelius, Jalmari Ruokokoski ja Henri Õunapuu.

title: Ribera ‘respectfully curious’ as to why a US judge spared Google
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Union should try to stay consistent with authorities elsewhere as it decides whether to order a breakup of Google’s advertising business, the bloc’s competition chief told POLITICO.

Teresa Ribera’s call for reflection marks a shift from the European Commission’s line a year ago that Google should break itself up, as the EU executive imposed a €2.95 billion fine for abuse of dominance in advertising. The U.S. search giant countered in November with a proposal of behavioral remedies only.

Her remarks on the need for regulatory alignment are especially significant as they come only days after a U.S. judge declined to force Google to sell its ad exchange.

“It’s always advisable to be sufficiently consistent, both for the companies, these global companies, the users and the regulators,” Ribera told POLITICO in an interview.

With the Trump administration threatening tariffs in response to EU enforcement while pursuing its own Big Tech crackdown, critics of America’s digital giants are starting to fear that pressure from an unpredictable U.S. could undermine Europe’s resolve to pursue its own agenda to rein in the dominant platforms.

content:
This press release contains information that some readers may find upsetting 

Meta failed to address harmful rhetoric on Facebook against the LGBTI community in Hungary by ineffectively applying its own moderation policies, a new Amnesty International briefing shows.  

‘It erodes my soul’: Meta’s contribution to anti-LGBTI discourse in Hungary, shows how Meta’s policy decisions, including the weakening of safeguards for high risk groups in January 2025 and the significant reduction in proactive content moderation, have negatively affected the LGBTI community in Hungary.

title: Sanandaj: Fereydoun Namdari and Sholeh Rouhi Arrested by Security Forces
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, two citizens have been arrested in Sanandaj.

The couple have been identified as Fereydoun Namdari, 55, and Sholeh Rouhi.

According to the report, on Sunday, September 6, approximately 15 Ministry of Intelligence agents went to Mr. Namdari’s workplace and arrested him by force and with violence, without presenting a judicial warrant. The agents subsequently went to his residence, conducted a thorough search of the premises, and arrested his wife, Sholeh Rouhi. She was also transferred to an undisclosed location.

At the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for their arrests, the charges brought against them, or their place of detention. The families’ efforts to obtain information about the couple’s condition and whereabouts have so far been unsuccessful.

title: Hungary Extends Abusive Migration State of Emergency
content:
Hungary’s government has extended until December 31 the “state of crisis caused by mass migration,” prolonging an emergency regime introduced in 2016 despite the absence of the conditions that could justify its continued use. 

Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced on September 4 that the government would extend the measure, which was due to expire on September 7. Magyar said the four-month extension would allow the government time to negotiate with European Union institutions on new legislation that would maintain strict border controls while complying with EU law.

The state of crisis enables exceptional measures—including summary removals of asylum seekers and migrants across the border fence without an individual procedure—that violate EU and human rights law.

title: Former Swiss Banker Handed Suspended Two-Year Sentence for Corruption
content:
A Swiss court has handed Pierre Mirabaud, a former president of the Swiss Bankers Association and former partner at the private bank Mirabaud & Cie, a two-year suspended prison sentence after finding him guilty of foreign bribery and money laundering.

The Swiss Federal Criminal Court delivered its verdict late Tuesday morning, state broadcaster SRF reported.

According to the indictment, the 78-year-old former banker "continuously and systematically" funneled nearly 300 payments totaling 82.3 million Swiss francs ($101.7 million) to a senior Kuwaiti government official between 2000 and 2012. In exchange, the Kuwaiti official allegedly invested $595.2 million with the Geneva-based private bank.

Mirabaud, who chaired the Swiss Bankers Association from 2003 to 2009, pleaded guilty to making the illicit payments and admitted to his role in the corruption and money-laundering scheme.

During the hearing, Mirabaud expressed remorse. “I am here to take responsibility; that's why I accepted this procedure,” he said, according to public broadcaster RTS.

title: State handouts, 10,000 lasers – and Trump’s election: six things we learned from the Elon Musk film
content:
Alex Gibney’s marathon documentary delivers numerous eye-raising insights into the broligarch’s business deals, early idealism and apocalyptic appetite for fathering children

Veteran documentarian Alex Gibney’s film about the richest broligarch on the planet has been one of the most eagerly anticipated films at the Venice film festival this year. The Oscar-winning 72-year-old, who has in previous films taken on the US military, the Catholic church, Vladimir Putin and Scientology, has been investigating the tech tycoon’s ascent and speaking to people in his orbit since late 2022, before his Maga turn and Trump 2.0.

The result clocks in at just under four hours and presents a comprehensive answer to how on earth one man managed to amass so much money and political influence. It is shocking less for any individual new pieces of information Gibney has unearthed than for its totality. Here are six things the film tells us:

title: Lapin yliopiston avajaiset: Suomi tarvitsee rohkeasti uudistuvia ja erikoistuvia yliopistoja
content:
Lapin yliopiston lukuvuoden 2026–2027 avajaisia vietettiin maanantaina 7. syyskuuta. Juhlan avajaispuheen piti rehtori Antti Syväjärvi, juhlapuheen Sitran yliasiamies Atte Jääskeläinen ja opiskelijan puheen LYYn hallituksen puheenjohtaja Inari Turkia. Puheissa painotettiin koulutukseen panostamisen ja uudistumisrohkeuden olevan Suomen kasvun edellytyksiä. Lisäksi muistutettiin opiskelijoiden taloudellisen tilanteen ja kohtuuhintaisen asumisen kehittämisestä ja siitä, että puheiden lisäksi tarvitaan myös jatkossa yhteistyötä ja konkreettisia toimia.

Rehtori Antti Syväjärvi painotti avajaispuheessaan, että suuret tavoitteet, kuten Suomen asema sivistyksen, demokratian ja tieteen vapauden edelläkävijänä, eivät saa jäädä vain tavoitteiksi paperilla. Tavoitteiden on muututtava päätöksiksi, rahoitukseksi ja korkeakoulujen mahdollisuudeksi tehdä työnsä hyvin. Syväjärvi totesi, että hyvin hoidettu korkeakoulu tuottaa hyvää elämää.

Hän kertasi puheessaan Korkeakoulutuksen ja tutkimuksen vision teesejä ja nosti niistä Lapin näkökulmasta keskeisiksi korkeakoulujen erikoistumisen ja yhteistyön vahvistamisen.

title: Gold OA reaches record 44pc share of global research output - Research Information
content:
"Gold open access (OA) articles reached their highest-ever share of global research output in 2025, accounting for 44% of all journal articles, reviews and conference papers published worldwide.

Nearly two million research articles were published through gold OA during the year, making it the principal driver of immediate, freely available access to research, according to the latest release of the STM Open Access Dashboard.

The Dashboard, which tracks the uptake of different routes to OA between 2015 and 2025, shows that gold OA has quadrupled over the past decade."

title: AI is helping gangs grow illicit tobacco networks, EU auditor warns
content:
Criminal gangs are using artificial intelligence to help them find locations in Europe to build illicit cigarette factories with less chance of getting caught, an EU auditor warned on Tuesday.

These gangs used to operate in Eastern Europe where it was easier to hide, Petri Sarvamaa in charge of the European Court of Auditor’s report on illicit tobacco, told a press briefing.

Now, with AI, it’s easier to find places to operate that are closer to their markets, he said, in rural locations and villages. “This reduces the risk in the supply chain for the criminals,” added Esther Torrente Heras, senior auditor.

It’s just one of the many challenges facing EU and member countries as they grapple to clamp down on illicit tobacco networks, which cause at least €13 billion in lost revenue in the bloc annually. In 2023, almost one in 10 cigarettes in Europe was illegally produced or smuggled in.

title: Durban Conference, 25 years on. Paul Divakar Namala: “Solidarity and resistance work in the long run”
content:
The third UN Conference Against Racism, Racial Discrimination, Xenophobia and Related Intolerance in 2001 was a watershed moment for millions across the world. Seven thousand people representing governments and civil society from 170 countries gathered in Durban, South Africa. Led by countries in the Global South, the Durban Conference challenged the idea that human rights is a Western concept, recognized the historical roots of contemporary forms of racism and called on States to repair the lasting consequences of colonialism and slavery. While the US and Israel withdrew from the Conference, the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action were adopted, both of which became foundational documents for the global fight against racism. But with racism still very much alive, we spoke with activists about their struggles and hopes. 

My name is Paul Divakar Namala. I am the Executive Director of The Inclusivity Project and Convenor of the Global Forum of Communities Discriminated on Work and Descent. My work focuses on communities whose social status, occupations and exclusion are inherited across generations through caste, analogous hierarchies and systems rooted in traditional slavery.
